findings.passage: By calling for universal background checks, a red flag law, safe storage requirements, and mandatory waiting periods for firearm purchases, Evers has aligned himself with the vast majority of our Wisconsin neighbors, who - regardless of who they voted for in the last election - overwhelmingly support these common-sense, life-saving measures.
findings.note: His statement on the governor's State of the State address, speaking for background checks on all sales, a red-flag law, safe storage rules and waiting periods.

findings.passage: We cannot change that now, but we can ensure that men and women struggling with depression and suicidal thoughts don’t have ready access to a gun. 85% of suicide attempts with a gun are successful versus less than 3% of attempts by drug overdose. Over 60% of all gun deaths in Wisconsin are by suicide.
findings.note: Same release; he links gun access to suicide and says laws should limit access for people in crisis, naming a friend and former legislator who died by suicide with a gun.
subjects: limit who may have a gun

findings.passage: Every suicide is preventable, and adding a waiting period … puts a barrier between somebody making an irrational decision and an irreversible harm,
findings.note: Quoted by WPR (the outlet quoted him; the ellipsis is in the outlet's text). He argues a waiting period would reduce impulsive homicides and suicides.

findings.passage: They rejected an amendment I offered which would have prevented individuals convicted of domestic violence from purchasing and possessing firearms.
findings.note: His statement (posted on Urban Milwaukee) after the last day of session: he offered an amendment barring people convicted of domestic violence from buying or having guns. The same release says Senate colleagues' amendments for universal background checks and a return of the 48-hour waiting period were also rejected.
subjects: limit who may have a gun

findings.passage: They even rejected an amendment that would require universal background checks for all gun purchases.
findings.note: Same release; he supports requiring background checks on all gun purchases.

findings.passage: Instead of focusing on ways to make our communities safer and implementing background checks for all types of firearm sales – which polling has shown a vast majority of the public and even 74% of National Rifle Association members support – Republicans took a completely irresponsible step backwards by ignoring the public safety and mental health needs of our community.
findings.note: His statement (posted on Urban Milwaukee) opposing repeal of the 48-hour handgun waiting period and calling for background checks on all firearm sales.

findings.passage: Instead of fighting this public health crisis, Republicans in control of the Legislature are proposing to give guns to teens with no training – an idea that is unwarranted, absurd, and dangerous.
findings.note: His statement (posted on Urban Milwaukee) opposing a bill that would put more handguns in teens' hands, skip concealed-carry training and allow more guns in school zones; he names stronger background check laws as the alternative.

findings.passage: The topics were quite varied, including healthcare, the environment, consumer protection, campaign finance, criminal justice reform, gun safety, worker rights, and - perhaps most important - public education.
findings.note: From his own newsletter wrapping up the 2025-26 session. He says the bills he co-sponsored covered many topics, gun safety among them. No bill number is given in this sentence. [kept from the first search pass]
subjects: general statement on gun safety laws

findings.passage: Two distinct, troubling ingredients of modern American life - extremism and gun violence - have come together to form a deadly cocktail, and the President and his allies have already begun to weaponize the latest example (the cowardly murder of right-wing personality Charlie Kirk) as a pretext to dismantle one of the most fundamental American freedoms - the freedom of speech.
findings.note: From his own newsletter after the killing of Charlie Kirk. He names gun violence as a troubling feature of American life; the passage is mainly about free speech and proposes no gun measure. [kept from the first search pass]
